html:
The Ruins of Saint Paul's are the stone front of the Jesuit church of the Mother of God in Macau, built from 1602 to about 1640. A fire in 1835 destroyed the rest of the church.

Beside it stood the Jesuit college of Saint Paul, the first Western style university in East Asia, which trained missionaries for China and Japan. Matteo Ricci prepared in Macau before entering China. Japanese Christians who fled persecution helped build the facade, which mixes European, Chinese and Japanese carving, with a ship, a dragon and Chinese characters.

It is the best known image of Portuguese Macau, held by Portugal from 1557, and part of the Historic Centre of Macau, a World Heritage Site since 2005. It stood through the decline of the Portuguese trade, the handover of 1999 and the casino boom.
